newsitem.title: USA: Cool, wet week slows Nebraska wheat seeding.
newsitem.headline: Cool, wet week slows Nebraska wheat seeding.

text.p: Cool, wet conditions impeded winter wheat plantings in Nebraska during the week ended Sunday and slowed corn and soybean development, according to the state's Agriculture Statistics Service.

Corn ratings improved slightly from the previous week with 32 percent rated excellent versus 26 the previous week. Fifty-three percent was rated good,, 12 fair, two poor and one very poor. About one percent of the crop had been harvested for grain versus none a year ago and the six average.
Harvest of corn for seed corn and silage advanced as did winter wheat seeding.

Soybeans improved with 31 percent rated excellent versus 23 the previous week. The rest of the crop was rated 48 percent good 18 fair and three poor. Statewide, 25 percent was dropping leaves versus 30 a year ago and the 55 average.
Sorghum rated 85 percent good to excellent, 13 percent fair, one poor and one very poor. Sorghum was 13 percent mature versus 16 a year ago and the 40 average.
Winter wheat was 44 percent planted versus 54 a year go and the 62 average.
Topsoils statewide were rated 27 percent surplus, 70 adequate and three short. Subsoil moisture was rated 10 percent surplus, 85 adequate and five short.
